response.text: Against Asuncion's hazy river skyline, the four hoist a shared terere thermos, passing it in a slow circle as a humid breeze snaps their linen culottes. When one gently brushes dust off another's bare shoulder, a third's jaw tightens - until she receives a deliberate cheek peck from the fourth, who then laces her fingers through all their hands, tugging them into a swaying group hug under the glowing cerro silhouette.

At Encarnacion's moonlit costanera, they kneel to trace the Parana's current with their fingertips, then stand and drape a single handwoven nanduti shawl across each other's backs. A possessive arm curl around one waist draws a sharp glance from the friend left out, but that friend leans in for a quick peck on the jealous one's temple, and they all step forward to clasp wrists, dipping their toes in unison at the water's foil-rippled edge.

On the Monday falls overlook, they steady their wide-brimmed hats against the spray-mist, then one re-ties another's slipping sandal strap while the other two watch - one with a quiet, flickering stare. The watched one responds by pecking the jealous woman's cheek, then pulls everyone into a four-way shoulder squeeze, their colorful aopo'i shirts brushing as they turn together to face the cascading foam, exhaling in sync.

At Cerro Tres Kandu's ridge, they pass a polished gourd of cool juice between them, then one loops her arm around the friend who shivers in the highland wind, tucking her closer. A sidelong glare from the rival flickers hotly until the shivering one pecks her on the corner of her mouth, after which all four link elbows and kick a pebble in a playful arc, watching it tumble toward the distant Ybytyruzu folds before laughing into the open sky.
